verdict.rationale: Sill's own docs say only paired devices can connect and that every connection is encrypted. They also say there is no server, so screen and keystrokes travel only between the user's devices. That is a bare first-party assertion, which is exactly what the story asks to go beyond: no cipher, key exchange, pairing protocol or wire format is described anywhere in the pack. Missing for 10: documented encryption protocol (key exchange, ciphers, pairing and authentication scheme), explicit end-to-end coverage across USB, direct wireless and Remote Access paths, independent or hands-on verification of the encryption.

support.subject: As an IT admin, sessions are encrypted end to end with the protocol documented, not just asserted

citations.quote: After that, only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.
There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
